transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janene Herbst.
President Trump is proposing new tariffs on 14 of the U.S.'s major trading partners,
including China, Japan, and the European Union,
saying it's to fight the other country's unfair trade practices.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben has more.
Well, they could go into effect within a couple of months.
That's what U.S. Trade Ambassador Jameson Greer said yesterday.
Now, as for what the rates will be, well, that's still unclear.
And that's because for each country accepting those additional tariffs on Brazil,
the White House has two rates they've listed, a proposed rate and a deal rate.
To give an example, the tariff on China could be 20 percent.
That's the deal rate.
But depending in part on how ongoing discussions go,
the rates on Chinese goods could go as high as 40 percent.
And here's Danielle Kurtzleben reporting.
In Southern California, flood advisories remain in effect
for a large swath of the coastline until after Thanksgiving.
And here's Kirk Sigler reports, many coastal communities hit hard
in recent months have scrambled to prepare for this so-called "king tide" event.
A now common sound of equipment dredging harbors and dozers pushing sand
onto beaches as the powerful El Nino has warmed the Pacific Ocean,
creating huge waves and sea levels a foot higher than normal.
Steps from the water and Huntington Beach cat Reeves has sandbags
four feet high around his apartment.
Only because this is the new, new times, this is what you got to do.
Reeves canceled his plans to fly to Texas to see his daughter for Thanksgiving
as he was worried about his place.
It's never the end of the world.
You know, it's just something you got to deal with and stuff.
But I love it here.
Presidents here say this week's king tide could be a test
for even larger swells predicted by Christmas.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News, Huntington Beach, California.
The first vaccines specifically designed to fight the Ebola outbreak,
currently spreading and the Democratic Republic of the Congo,
are poised to enter a clinical trial in that country.
As NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports, the vaccine could be key
to controlling the outbreak.
Regulators in DRC are poised to OK two new Ebola vaccines for testing.
One is an mRNA vaccine made by Moderna.
The other was developed by the University of Oxford.
In the outbreak's very early days,
both vaccine candidates were fast-tracked with millions of dollars
by a vaccine nonprofit called the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations.
Researchers are already testing whether an existing Ebola vaccine,
designed for a different kind of Ebola, can offer protection.
It'll likely be some time before researchers get any results.
Conducting a clinical trial in this region,
where there's lots of armed conflict, is challenging.
But if the vaccine is effective,
it could help bring the fastest spreading Ebola outbreak ever to an end.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
This is NPR.
EU leaders are working to bridge major differences
over the bloc's long-term budget,
trying to agree on a new major loan to support Ukraine.
The 2028-34 budget could amount to between 1 and 1.2%
of the bloc's gross national income.
European Council President Antonio Acosta says leaders,
at the two-day meeting in Brussels,
have the responsibility to find a balanced budget agreement
that will allow the EU to take on challenges ahead.
But complicating things?
Upcoming elections in Spain this weekend,
and next year in France, Italy, and Poland.
The EU is divided on more defense spending
over Russia's nearly five-year-old war in Ukraine.
Thanksgiving is also celebrated in Liberia and West Africa.
It started in the 19th century when Black Americans were resettled there
and brought the holiday with them.
Ari Daniel has more.
The Liberian legislature established Thanksgiving in 1883,
when the country managed to maintain its sovereignty
despite British land incursions.
"It's steeped in religious gratitude," says Ivan Kephart-Wia.
"It's giving thanks to God for our freedom, for divine protection.
It giving thanks to God for unity and for the harvest."
Wia's celebration starts in the morning at church.
The subsequent meal varies between households,
but her family serves jolliff rice, chicken, watermelon, and stews.
She says she's grateful for peace and security
in a country rocked by civil wars between 1989 and the early 2000s.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, Japan, and EU
Southern California flood advisories remain in effect through Thanksgiving amid king tides
Huntington Beach resident Cat Reeves sandbags apartment, cancels Thanksgiving trip over flooding
Regulators in DRC poised to approve Moderna and Oxford Ebola vaccines for clinical trials
EU leaders struggle to agree on long-term budget and Ukraine loan at Brussels summit
Liberia celebrates Thanksgiving, a holiday brought by resettled Black Americans in 19th century
